topic: Why leap years skip some century years

sources.title: Which years are leap years and can you have leap seconds?
Did a Calendar Change Cause Riots in England?

facts.claim: The solar year, which sets the seasons, lasts about 365.2422 days.
A common calendar year has 365 days, so without leap days the calendar would slip about a quarter of a day each year against the seasons.
The Julian calendar added a leap day every 4 years, which made its average year 365.25 days, slightly too long.
By the 1500s that small surplus had added up to about 10 days.
In 1582 Pope Gregory XIII introduced the Gregorian calendar and dropped 10 days: Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed by Friday 15 October.
In the Gregorian calendar a century year is a leap year only if it divides by 400: 1600 and 2000 were leap years, 1700, 1800 and 1900 were not, and 2100 will not be.
Britain switched in 1752: Wednesday 2 September was followed by Thursday 14 September, skipping 11 days.
Skipping three century leap days every 400 years removes the Julian calendar's excess of about three days per 400 years.

misconceptions: a leap year is simply every 4 years
